featured_videos.creator: Steak and Butter Gal
featured_videos.editorial_title: This Is The New Butter (And You’ll Be FORCED To Eat It!)
featured_videos.commentary: Okay, so the community is fired up about this one, and honestly, they're not wrong. The "Bill Gates" and "FDA conspiracy" energy is strong in the comments, but underneath all that frustration is a real question: what's actually changing in our food supply, and should we care? Here's the thing. whether you're full carnivore or just protective of your butter, this hits different because butter is supposed to be simple. It's one of the few foods we thought was non-negotiable. The local farm comment really resonates though. Community is saying they're done trusting labels and moving toward direct sourcing, which honestly tracks with what I'm seeing across carnivore spaces. People aren't waiting for regulatory clarity anymore; they're just finding their own butter suppliers and moving on.

featured_videos.title: This Carnivore Recipe Destroyed My Carb Cravings
featured_videos.creator: Steak and Butter Gal
featured_videos.editorial_title: This Carnivore Recipe Destroyed My Carb Cravings
featured_videos.commentary: The thing about carb cravings is they're not really about willpower, they're about satisfaction. When you find a recipe that actually delivers on taste and texture without leaving you wanting more, everything shifts. What I've seen work with my coaching clients is that these kinds of wins early on make the whole transition stick, because you're not white-knuckling through deprivation. A $5 recipe that kills the cravings? That's not just convenient, it's permission to stop feeling like you're missing out. Budget-friendly wins like this are exactly what gets people past those first few weeks when they're most likely to quit.

featured_videos.title: Carnivore/Lion Diet Update: Not Carnivore Anymore?
featured_videos.creator: Mikhaila Peterson
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivore/Lion Diet Update: Not Carnivore Anymore?
featured_videos.commentary: Mikhaila's update hits on something I see constantly in my coaching: the carnivore diet isn't always the final destination, it's often the starting point. After eight years of strict lion diet, her ability to reintroduce plants without triggering arthritis or depression is actually a win, not a failure. The real work was getting her body healed enough to tolerate variety again. This is why I always tell people that your day-one carnivore approach might not be your day-365 approach, and that's okay. What matters most is listening to your own body rather than treating any diet like dogma.

featured_videos.title: Just 1 TSP Kills Cortisol & Makes You Sleep 8 Hours Straight
featured_videos.creator: Steak and Butter Gal
featured_videos.editorial_title: Just 1 TSP Kills Cortisol & Makes You Sleep 8 Hours Straight
featured_videos.commentary: The comment section here nails what actually matters. People aren't just talking about the one teaspoon trick, they're sharing real transformations, cortisol breakthroughs, and the simple shift from viewing food as entertainment to fuel. That's the pattern we're seeing across the carnivore community right now, and it changes everything about how people approach the diet. What's striking is how many mention getting off medications they thought were permanent, which tells you something about the power of addressing root causes like cortisol and micronutrient deficiencies instead of just treating symptoms. The iodine confusion in the comments is a good reminder to check transcripts, but it also shows people are actually experimenting and paying attention to the details that move the needle on sleep and stress.

featured_videos.title: New Study DESTROYS What Everyone Thought About Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Max German
featured_videos.editorial_title: New Study DESTROYS What Everyone Thought About Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: Most of the "carnivore concerns" circulating online come from people who've never actually tried it or stuck with it long enough to see what happens. When a new study drops that challenges the mainstream narrative, it matters because it's one more data point saying what we're already seeing in practice. The real question isn't whether carnivore works, it's why so many people are willing to dismiss evidence just because it doesn't fit the conventional wisdom. If you've been on the fence because you heard it would wreck your health, this is worth watching with an open mind.
